title: Tribunal upholds £60,000 fine on DPP Law over 2022 breach of 682 clients' data
date_note: Legal Futures published on 20 November 2026 and gives no decision date; the attack was in early June 2022.
place: United Kingdom (offices in Merseyside, Birmingham and London; city not stated)
geo_basis: country, as the source gives no single city
summary: Legal Futures reports that the First-tier Tribunal dismissed DPP Law's appeal against a £60,000 fine from the Information Commission. A June 2022 cyber-attack on an unrestricted legacy administrator account published sensitive details of 682 clients on the dark web. The tribunal found DPP failed to implement appropriate technical and organisational measures and notified the regulator 43 days after the attack.
plain: A tribunal has refused a law firm's appeal against a £60,000 data-protection fine after a 2022 attack exposed 682 clients' sensitive details.
exec: Regulators and tribunals hold firms liable for unmanaged legacy systems and late breach reporting.
action: Review administrator accounts on legacy systems, their privileges and whether they are still needed and secure, and report breaches to the regulator promptly.
impact: Details of 682 clients published on the dark web in 2022.

validation.note: Single publisher (Legal Futures) reporting the First-tier Tribunal decision; the BAILII decision itself was not read.
